title: Gather the scattered
hook: sound the great shofar for freedom and gather the scattered

segments.voice: Yesterday, the blessing of the years. Your line was bless the year. Did one piece of work get done with care? Today, the Amidah turns from the private to the whole people. Day five hundred eighty-seven.

Pull up a map of where Jewish families have lived. Babylon and Baghdad. Cordoba and Toledo. Fez, Cairo, Aleppo, Sana'a. Vilna, Kraków, Odessa. Cochin on the coast of India. Then Brooklyn, Buenos Aires, Johannesburg, Melbourne. Ask almost any Jewish family where their great-grandparents were born and you'll often get a different country from where they live now, sometimes two or three. For many centuries, every weekday, there's been a line in the Amidah that speaks directly to that map.
screen: `BABYLON, CORDOBA, FEZ, VILNA.` → `COCHIN, BROOKLYN, BUENOS AIRES.` → `A LINE THAT SPEAKS TO THE MAP.`

segments.voice: The tenth blessing says: sound the great shofar for our freedom. Raise a banner to gather our exiles, and gather us together from the four corners of the earth. Blessed are You, who gathers the dispersed of Your people Israel. The great shofar comes from the prophet Isaiah. In the old Jewish translation: "it shall come to pass in that day, that a great horn shall be blown," and the lost and the scattered come home to worship in Jerusalem. The banner comes from Isaiah too: a signal raised high, so people far away can see where to come. Notice the first word of the blessing is not gather. It's teka: blow. The shofar is the sound of the Jubilee year, when slaves went free and land returned to its families. So freedom comes first, then gathering. This is the first of the Amidah's requests for the whole people's future, a turn from my troubles to our story. The Talmud, in Megillah 17b, says it follows the blessing of the years because a prophet promised that when the land bears fruit again, the exiles will be near. For centuries, Jews said these words in places where they could never imagine going back. In the twentieth century, many saw the return of Jews to the land of Israel in this light, and others still read the blessing as pointing to a future not yet here. Either way, every weekday, scattered people ask to be gathered.
screen: `TEKA: BLOW THE GREAT SHOFAR.` · `RAISE A BANNER FOR THE EXILES.` · `FREEDOM FIRST, THEN GATHERING.` · `FROM MY TROUBLES TO OUR STORY.` · then, large: `GATHER THE SCATTERED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: think of someone far away. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind someone you love who lives far from you: a sibling across the country, a grandparent in another land, a friend who moved and slowly went quiet. Picture where they are right now, what time it is there, what they might be doing. Imagine, for a moment, the whole table together again. If you pray, you can hold them in this blessing. The bell holds the time.
Gather the scattered. The Amidah's tenth blessing: sound the great shofar for freedom, and gather the exiles from the four corners of the earth.
Your line: gather the scattered. Today, reach out to the far-away person you pictured, and make one plan, however small, to be in the same place. Day five hundred eighty-seven.

howItsDone: Teka beshofar, the request to gather the exiles, is the tenth blessing of the weekday Amidah, said three times a day; communities differ in how they relate it to the modern State of Israel.

trapdoor: what you thought: an old line about going back to Israel.
what it means: freedom first, then gathering: scattered people asking, every weekday, to be one people again.
what a scholar hears: Isaiah 27:13 for the great horn, Isaiah 11:12 for the banner and four corners; the Jubilee shofar of Leviticus 25; Megillah 17b on Ezekiel 36:8.
